summary:
Team Grigori developed and built an interactive Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) visualization platform for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. The web application, built with Next.js, Tailwind CSS and Three.js, processes multi-temporal satellite data to visualize surface deformation at centimeter resolution, flood inundation and tectonic shifts.

Our platform makes sense of it all, translating complex phase difference and L-band/S-band radar telemetry from NISAR and other missions into easy-to-understand 3D maps that can see through clouds.

This project is important because it transforms raw satellite data into insights that are accessible and actionable. It helps researchers and local communities in vulnerable areas such as the Western Ghats to actively monitor landslides and environmental changes, thus improving climate resilience and disaster response.
details:
Team Grigori’s NASA Space Apps project is an interactive platform that visualizes Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) telemetry from the NISAR. Built with Next.js, Three.js, and Python, it handles Differential Interferometry (DInSAR) for centimeter-scale land deformation and flooding mapping.

Benefits & Impact: Vulnerable communities in regions like the Western Ghats can take proactive action on landslides and climate risks through cloud-penetrating radar insights.

Creativity & Considerations: We merged complex aerospace data with immersive 3D web storytelling, balancing scientific rigor with accessible UI design for non-experts to enable real-world disaster resilience.
